An accurate measurement data will produce good track estimates. However, in a real-world scenario, none of the measurements are perfect due to several factors, like the resolution of the sensor, noise and inaccuracies originating from external influences. Uncertainties in the measurements will degrade the performance of any trackers. Ignoring some of the errors in the measurements for simplicity may lead to wrong spatial perception.

articleTitle: Use of Magnetic Positioning Systems in Industrial and Biomedical Applications
abstract: Nowadays the ability to locate people and objects is becoming an important and necessary aspect for the wide range of applications concerning localization-based services. Indeed, applications based on spatial and time awareness of people and objects within certain contexts are being developed. Some application examples in which the positioning problem must be considered and solved are: industrial automation, virtual reality, smart cities, smart health, robot navigation and remote surgery. Although in outdoor environments this does not represent a big issue thanks to the presence and support of Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSSs), there is a whole series of scenarios, such as indoors, underground, and underwater environments, in which GNSSs fail due to the complexity of the considered environments with respect to radio propagation. Nowadays, in the considered scenarios, the identification of a reliable method able to satisfy the positioning requirements is an open issue, for which the measurement community can provide a valuable contribution regarding the proposal of measurement methods and procedures, the evaluation of the major causes of uncertainty of the devices and the consideration of these features within positioning algorithms and data processing.

articleTitle: Insect-Inspired Spiking Neural Controllers for Adaptive Behaviors in Bio-Robots
abstract: The perception-action loop is at the basis of living beings' behavior and still represents a challenging process to be modeled, due to its complexity both at the level of the input sensory system and the output behavioral repertoire, determined by the real-life constraints imposed by the environment.

articleTitle: Editorial: 25 Years of Instrumentation & Measurement Magazine!
abstract: Dear Readers, This issue will complete 25 years of publication of IEEE Instrumentation & Measurement Magazine! I am really honored to handle the activity related to generating this Magazine, and I would like to give recognition and appreciation to past Editors in Chief, the Editorial Assistants, authors and reviewers, and the whole staff who have supported the production activity during these 25 years.

Welcome, dearest members of the IEEE Instrumentation and Measurement Society. A new year is starting after we all have been dragged into a completely new world and we all were forced to face unexpected threats. The IEEE Instrumentation and Measurement Society has crossed these two last years by striving to offer the best possible services to our valued members. Our conferences, even if held in a virtual manner, have been largely populated and attended as have our other events including Virtual Distinguished Lectures and Video Tutorials.

articleTitle: Metrology for All: Women in Metrology (WIM): 2022 First Forum
abstract: Women in Science, Technology Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) initiatives have been emphasized in recent years because of the “glass ceiling” that still exists to this day. Within these efforts, it is vital to always observe that depending on where you are born/grew up/work, to be a successful woman in Engineering and Science can be an even higher mountain to climb [1].

articleTitle: Guest Editorial: I&M Around the World: Highlighting China of IEEE Region 10, Part B
abstract: In the April 2022 issue of Instrumentation & Measurement Magazine, some researchers' works related to instrumentation and measurement in China were introduced. Here, we continue to share with readers some other works that were conducted in China.

articleTitle: Guest Editorial: Biomimetic Architectures: Sensing and Control
abstract: Biomimetics relies on the research and development of new theories and related methodologies based on a solid biological, nature-inspired background, focused to improve existing technologies. This Special Issue of Instrumentation & Measurement Magazine concentrates on examples of bio-inspired solutions and the related mechanisms and principles to model parts of, or the whole, sensing-perception-action loop, spanning from the vegetable to the animal kingdom. These realms contain extremely efficient examples in this sense, yet details in charge of this efficiency are largely unknown. To build efficient bio-inspired artefacts as a whole, bio-inspired robots are the main center of interest; however, bio-robot design and realization involve a large number of different disciplines which play relevant roles within the selected papers in this Special Issue. In particular, five papers have been accepted for publication, reflecting several aspects of the fields mentioned above by covering different areas of bio-inspired sensing, modeling and control. Some of the contributions focus more on the sensing aspects whereas others on modeling and control. The variety of selected papers reflects the efforts made by all authors to focus either on methodological aspects or technical issues. Some contributions are in the form of surveys and reflect the authors' experience in the respective fields.

articleTitle: Guest Editorial: Special Issue on Measurements, Sensors and Standards in Modern Communication Networks
abstract: In the last years, communication networks have become a central piece for many applications in multiple domains, including commercial and industrial systems, personal care and medicine, modern vehicles and vehicular networks, and environmental and disaster early-warning monitoring, to cite a few examples. Each application field has specific constraints regarding data rate, connectivity, security, immunity to electromagnetic disturbances, coverage area, and power consumption. Therefore, designers and researchers are continuously engaged in new challenges for reaching the expected targets in terms of performance and actual applicability in the field while considering the costs and requirements in designing suitable architectures warranting scalability, the required level of security and effective maintainability, and resilience.

articleTitle: Guest Editorial: I&M Around the World: Highlighting China from IEEE Region 10
abstract: With the rapid development of science and technology, there is also increasing advancement in instrumentation and measurement in China in recent years. It is a great pleasure for me to highlight some of those advancements and show the rest of the world that China is undergoing fast changes in this field.

We currently live in a world full of intelligent sensors. These intelligent sensors almost control our lives as our everyday activities now depend on the data provided by such sensors. For instance, our smart devices monitor our heart rate, our daily activities, and our sleep. They alert us to conduct various activities and connect us to either health care providers when there are medical alerts. There now exist self-driving cars which are able to make intelligent decisions like human beings while driving on the road. Thus, devices and machines are not only becoming intelligent but are also becoming autonomous.

Technical Committees (TC) are one of the most important parts of research advancements for all IEEE societies, and the Instrumentation and Measurement Society (IMS) is not an exception from this point of view. The IMS has 23 active TCs, whose subjects range from condition monitoring to wireless measurements. We present this issue of the Instrumentation & Measurement Magazine to explain to any reader the research types carried out by the IMS, and we asked all of the TC Chairs to explain the type of research they are carrying out in their TC. This year, you will find six research areas corresponding to different TCs.

articleTitle: Guest Editorial: The “Read our Videos-Watch our Papers” Initiative of the IEEE Instrumentation & Measurement Magazine and Video Tutorial Program
abstract: We are glad to publish, in this issue of the Instrumentation & Measurement Magazine (IMM) a collection of contributions from an initiative between the Magazine and the Video Tutorial program of the Instrumentation and Measurement Society. The initiative is named “Read our Videos-Watch our Papers,” and it aims at collecting contributions from speakers who already recorded Video Tutorials for the Society. The video collection can be found at https://ieee-ims.org/vtprogram, where about thirty videos have been collected so far. The papers published in this issue are twins to some videos we have in the I&M collection. We believe that this is a valuable oppportunity to improve the impact of both the videos and the corresponding papers. The action is intended to work both ways, and papers published in this issue are the first group of contributions we have collected so far. I do thank the authors for collaborating in this effort. The initiative has not concluded, of course, and I hope that both the videos and number of papers will grow in the near future. We encourage interested authors to propose videos to the Video Tutotial Progam and corresponding papers to the IMM, so that we can consider the contribution as part of the initative.
